lesson_scope: Chords in circles, isosceles triangle bisectors, triangle area 0.5*r^2*sin(theta), minor and major segment areas 0.5*r^2*(theta - sin(theta)), segment perimeters, and multi-segment composite regions.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: direct chord length calculation using half-angle sine ratio.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of the chord formula AB = 2r*sin(theta/2).

hints: Bisect the isosceles triangle formed by the two radii and the chord.
The half-angle at the centre is $\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
Use $\sin(\pi/3) = \dfrac{AB/2}{12}$, so $AB = 2(12)\sin(\pi/3) = 24\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 12\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.

walkthrough.text:
Bisect the vertex angle of the isosceles triangle $\triangle OAB$ to form two congruent right-angled triangles:
$$\text{Half-angle } = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$$

Apply the sine ratio to find the chord length $AB$:
$$AB = 2r\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = 2(12)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$$

Substitute the exact trigonometric value $\sin(\pi/3) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:
$$AB = 24 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 12\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies chord formula $AB = 2(12)\sin(\pi/3)$ or cosine rule $AB^2 = 12^2 + 12^2 - 2(12^2)\cos(2\pi/3)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: direct triangle area calculation using two radii and sine of central angle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of the triangle area formula Area = 0.5*r^2*sin(theta).

hints: Use the triangle area formula $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ with $a = b = r = 8\text{ cm}$ and $C = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.
Substitute into $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}(8^2)\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$.
Evaluate $\sin(\pi/6) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ to find $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}(64)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 16\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text:
State the triangle area formula for an angle enclosed by two radii:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta$$

Substitute $r = 8\text{ cm}$ and $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(8^2)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{2}(64)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$$

Simplify the arithmetic:
$$\text{Area} = 32 \times \frac{1}{2} = 16\text{ cm}^2$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: direct minor segment area calculation subtracting triangle area from sector area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of segment area A = 0.5*r^2*(theta - sin(theta)).

hints: The area of a circular segment is found by subtracting the triangle area from the sector area: $A = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta)$.
Substitute $r = 10$ and $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ into $A = \dfrac{1}{2}(10^2)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)$.
Use $\sin(\pi/3) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ to write the exact area: $50\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{50\pi}{3} - 25\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text:
State the segment area formula:
$$A_{\text{segment}} = \text{Area}(\text{Sector}) - \text{Area}(\triangle OAB) = \frac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta)$$

Substitute $r = 10\text{ cm}$ and $\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}(10^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) = 50\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$$

Expand to standard exact form:
$$A = \frac{50\pi}{3} - 25\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains exact value $\dfrac{50\pi}{3} - 25\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$ (or equivalent exact form).

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: minor segment perimeter calculation adding curved arc length and straight chord.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of segment perimeter P = s + chord.

hints: The perimeter of a segment consists of the curved arc plus the straight chord: $P = s + c$.
Find the arc length: $s = r\theta = 6\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 3\pi\text{ cm}$.
Find the chord length: $c = 2(6)\sin(\pi/4) = 12\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$, then sum $3\pi + 6\sqrt{2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the arc length $s$ bounding the segment:
$$s = r\theta = 6 \times \frac{\pi}{2} = 3\pi\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the chord length $c$ bounding the segment:
$$c = 2r\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = 2(6)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 12 \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$$

Add the two boundary components to find the perimeter:
$$P = s + c = (3\pi + 6\sqrt{2})\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates arc length $3\pi$ and chord length $6\sqrt{2}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: inverse recovery of acute central angle from triangle area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving Area = 0.5*r^2*sin(theta) for theta.

hints: Set up the triangle area equation: $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta = 9$.
Substitute $r = 6$: $\dfrac{1}{2}(36)\sin\theta = 18\sin\theta = 9$.
Divide by $18$ to get $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$, and state the exact acute angle in radians: $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

walkthrough.text:
State the triangle area formula with $r = 6\text{ cm}$ and $\text{Area} = 9\text{ cm}^2$:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta \implies 9 = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)\sin\theta$$

Simplify and isolate $\sin\theta$:
$$9 = 18\sin\theta \implies \sin\theta = \frac{9}{18} = \frac{1}{2}$$

Since $\theta$ is an acute angle ($0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}$):
$$\theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: major segment area calculation by subtracting minor segment from total circle area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of major segment area = circle area - minor segment area.

hints: A chord divides a circle into a minor segment and a major segment. Their areas sum to the total area of the circle.
Calculate the total area of the circle: $A_{\text{circle}} = \pi r^2 = \pi(4^2) = 16\pi\text{ cm}^2$.
Subtract the minor segment area: $A_{\text{major}} = 16\pi - (4\pi - 8) = 12\pi + 8\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the total area of the circle of radius $r = 4\text{ cm}$:
$$A_{\text{circle}} = \pi r^2 = \pi(4^2) = 16\pi\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the minor segment area from the complete circle area to obtain the major segment area:
$$A_{\text{major}} = A_{\text{circle}} - A_{\text{minor}}$$
$$A_{\text{major}} = 16\pi - (4\pi - 8)$$

Expand and simplify the exact expression:
$$A_{\text{major}} = 16\pi - 4\pi + 8 = (12\pi + 8)\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates circle area $16\pi$ and subtracts minor segment area: $16\pi - (4\pi - 8)$.
Obtains exact major segment area $(12\pi + 8)\text{ cm}^2$.

hints: Join the chord endpoints to the centre to form an isosceles triangle with two sides of length $10\text{ cm}$.
Bisect the triangle: the vertex angle becomes $\pi/6$, the hypotenuse is $10\text{ cm}$, and the opposite side is $AB/2$.
Use $\sin(\pi/6) = (AB/2)/10$, so $AB = 20\sin(\pi/6) = 10\text{ cm}$.

walkthrough.text: Join the centre $O$ to chord endpoints $A$ and $B$. In triangle $\triangle OAB$, $OA = OB = 10\text{ cm}$ and vertex angle $\angle AOB = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.
Drop a perpendicular from $O$ to chord $AB$. This bisects the chord into halves of length $\frac{AB}{2}$ and bisects the central angle to $\frac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$.

Apply the sine ratio in one of the right-angled halves:
$$\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{\frac{AB}{2}}{10} \implies AB = 20\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$$

Evaluate using $\sin(\pi/6) = \frac{1}{2}$:
$$AB = 20 \times \frac{1}{2} = 10\text{ cm}$$
(Notice that an angle of $\frac{\pi}{3}$ between two equal sides forms an equilateral triangle, confirming $AB = 10\text{ cm}$).

hints: The minor segment area is sector area minus triangle area: $A = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta)$.
Substitute $r = 6$ and $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ into $A = \dfrac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)$.
Evaluate $\sin(\pi/2) = 1$ to obtain $18\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1\right) = 9\pi - 18\text{ cm}^2$.

walkthrough.text:
State the formula for minor segment area:
$$A = \text{Area}(\text{Sector}) - \text{Area}(\text{Triangle}) = \frac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta)$$

Substitute $r = 6\text{ cm}$ and $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\text{ radians}$:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right) = 18\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - 1\right)$$

Expand to obtain exact area:
$$A = 9\pi - 18\text{ cm}^2$$

hints: The perimeter of the minor segment is the sum of the curved arc length and the straight chord length: $P = s + c$.
Calculate arc length using $s = r\theta = 8(1.1) = 8.8\text{ cm}$.
Calculate chord length using $c = 2r\sin(\theta/2) = 2(8)\sin(0.55) = 16\sin(0.55)$, then sum and round to $3$ significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the arc length $s$ of the minor sector:
$$s = r\theta = 8 \times 1.1 = 8.8\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the chord length $c$ by bisecting the central angle:
$$c = 2r\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = 2(8)\sin\left(\frac{1.1}{2}\right) = 16\sin(0.55)$$

Evaluate the chord length using radian mode:
$$16\sin(0.55) \approx 16 \times 0.522687 = 8.3630\text{ cm}$$

Sum the arc and chord lengths to determine total segment perimeter:
$$P = s + c = 8.8 + 8.3630 = 17.1630\text{ cm}$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $P = 17.2\text{ cm}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $17.163\dots$ and rounds to $17.2\text{ cm}$ (3 s.f.).

hints: Bisect the chord of length $12\text{ cm}$ into two halves of length $6\text{ cm}$.
Use $\sin(\theta/2) = \dfrac{6}{10} = 0.6$, then double $\sin^{-1}(0.6)$ to find the full central angle $\theta$.
Use $A = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta) = 50(\theta - \sin\theta)$ with unrounded $\theta$, then round both answers to $3$ significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Drop a perpendicular from the circle centre $O$ to the chord. This bisects the chord to $6\text{ cm}$ and bisects the angle to $\frac{\theta}{2}$:
$$\sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = \frac{6}{10} = 0.6$$

Solve for the central angle $\theta$ in radians:
$$\frac{\theta}{2} = \sin^{-1}(0.6) \approx 0.643501\text{ rad} \implies \theta = 2(0.643501) = 1.287002\text{ rad}$$
Rounding to $3$ decimal places / $4$ significant figures gives $\theta = 1.287\text{ radians}$.

Calculate the minor segment area using $A = \frac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta)$:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}(10^2)(1.287002 - \sin(1.287002)) = 50(1.287002 - 0.96)$$

Evaluate the area:
$$A = 50(0.327002) = 16.3501\text{ cm}^2$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $A = 16.4\text{ cm}^2$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $16.350\dots$ and rounds to $16.4\text{ cm}^2$ (3 s.f.).

hints: First find the minor sector area and minor triangle area with $\theta = 2\pi/3$ and $r = 4\text{ cm}$.
Minor sector area is $\dfrac{1}{2}(4^2)(2\pi/3) = \dfrac{16\pi}{3}$, and triangle area is $\dfrac{1}{2}(4^2)\sin(2\pi/3) = 4\sqrt{3}$.
Subtract minor segment $\left(\dfrac{16\pi}{3} - 4\sqrt{3}\right)$ from the full circle area $\pi(4^2) = 16\pi$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the area of the minor sector with central angle $\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}$:
$$A_{\text{minor sector}} = \frac{1}{2}(4^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{16\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of the triangle $\triangle OAB$:
$$A_{\text{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2}(4^2)\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 8 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Determine the minor segment area:
$$A_{\text{minor segment}} = \frac{16\pi}{3} - 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the minor segment area from the complete circle area $A_{\text{circle}} = \pi(4^2) = 16\pi$:
$$A_{\text{major segment}} = 16\pi - \left(\frac{16\pi}{3} - 4\sqrt{3}\right)$$
$$A_{\text{major segment}} = \left(16\pi - \frac{16\pi}{3}\right) + 4\sqrt{3} = \left(\frac{32\pi}{3} + 4\sqrt{3}\right)\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Subtracts from circle area $16\pi$ to obtain $\dfrac{32\pi}{3} + 4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$.

hints: Use the chord equation $14 = 2r\sin(1.4/2) = 2r\sin(0.7)$ to find $r = \dfrac{7}{\sin(0.7)}$.
Compute segment area using $A = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(1.4 - \sin(1.4))$ with your unrounded radius value.
Compute segment perimeter using $P = 14 + r(1.4)$, then round all three quantities to $3$ significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the chord length formula to solve for the radius $r$:
$$14 = 2r\sin\left(\frac{1.4}{2}\right) = 2r\sin(0.7)$$
$$r = \frac{14}{2\sin(0.7)} = \frac{7}{\sin(0.7)} \approx 10.86588\text{ cm}$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $r = 10.9\text{ cm}$.

Calculate the minor segment area using the unrounded radius $r$:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}r^2(1.4 - \sin(1.4)) = \frac{1}{2}(10.86588)^2(1.4 - \sin(1.4))$$
$$A = \frac{1}{2}(118.0674)(1.4 - 0.985450) = 59.0337(0.414550) \approx 24.4724\text{ cm}^2$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $A = 24.5\text{ cm}^2$.

Calculate the perimeter of the segment (chord plus arc length):
$$P = \text{chord} + s = 14 + r(1.4) = 14 + 10.86588(1.4) = 14 + 15.2122 = 29.2122\text{ cm}$$
Rounding to $3$ significant figures gives $P = 29.2\text{ cm}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains area $24.472\dots$ and rounds to $24.5\text{ cm}^2$ (3 s.f.).
Obtains perimeter $29.212\dots$ and rounds to $29.2\text{ cm}$ (3 s.f.).

hints: Set up the total arc length equation: $r\alpha + r(2\alpha) = 18\text{ cm}$ with $r = 6\text{ cm}$.
Solve $6(3\alpha) = 18$ to find $\alpha = 1\text{ radian}$.
Find the areas of the two minor segments: $\dfrac{1}{2}(6^2)(1 - \sin 1) = 18(1 - \sin 1)$ and $18(2 - \sin 2)$, and subtract their sum from the circle area $36\pi$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the sum of the two minor arc lengths with radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$:
$$s_1 + s_2 = r\alpha + r(2\alpha) = 6\alpha + 12\alpha = 18\alpha$$
$$18\alpha = 18 \implies \alpha = 1\text{ radian}$$
Check validity: $\alpha = 1 < \pi$ and $2\alpha = 2 < \pi$, so both chords enclose valid non-overlapping minor segments.

Calculate the area of the first minor segment ($	heta_1 = 1$):
$$A_1 = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)(1 - \sin 1) = 18(1 - \sin 1)\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of the second minor segment ($	heta_2 = 2$):
$$A_2 = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)(2 - \sin 2) = 18(2 - \sin 2)\text{ cm}^2$$

Sum the two removed segment areas:
$$A_1 + A_2 = 18(1 - \sin 1 + 2 - \sin 2) = 18(3 - \sin 1 - \sin 2)\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract from the total area of the circle ($A_{\text{circle}} = \pi(6^2) = 36\pi$):
$$A_{\text{remaining}} = 36\pi - 18(3 - \sin 1 - \sin 2)\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains $\alpha = 1$, verifying both angles $\alpha = 1$ and $2\alpha = 2$ lie in $(0, \pi)$.
Sums the two segment areas to obtain $18(3 - \sin 1 - \sin 2)$.
Subtracts the sum of segments from circle area to obtain $36\pi - 18(3 - \sin 1 - \sin 2)\text{ cm}^2$.
